concepts.concept: Instruction fetch result that this block delivers to the bus (the 32-bit instruction word driven out)
concepts.writers: rdata is driven from ROM or RAM depending on generics: rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr)) (line 81, IMEM_INIT=true, not alt_style) or rdata <= mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr_ff)) (line 95, IMEM_INIT=true, alt_style); when IMEM_INIT=false rdata(7..0)..rdata(31..24) are assigned from mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3 at lines 128-131 (default) or 159-162 (alt_style). The RAM bytes mem_ram_b0..b3 themselves are written from bus_req_i.data at lines 116/119/122/125 (default writes) or 145/148/151/154 (alternative) under the write guard (if (bus_req_i.stb='1') and (bus_req_i.rw='1') at line 114 or 143) and gated by the byte-enable bits bus_req_i.ben(0..3) (lines 115/118/121/124 or 144/147/150/153).
concepts.observers: External observation is via the response port: bus_rsp_o.data is driven with rdata when rden='1' (line 185), so fetched instruction words exit the module on bus_rsp_o.data (line 185).

confidentiality.reason: rdata is presented on the external port bus_rsp_o.data when rden='1' (line 185), so an external observer can read fetched instructions and the integrator may treat those instruction words as confidential.

integrity.reason: RAM bytes that feed rdata are written from bus_req_i.data under the write guard (if (bus_req_i.stb='1') and (bus_req_i.rw='1') at line 114 with per-byte assigns at lines 116/119/122/125 and 145/148/151/154), so an external bus master can modify the instruction contents that rdata later delivers (line 185); whether that writer is trusted depends on integration.

availability.reason: the read-enable rden is set from bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) at line 176) and bus_rsp_o.data is driven only when rden='1' (line 185), so external bus_req_i inputs can block instruction delivery.

undermined behavior.reason: bus_rsp_o.data is driven only from rdata (line 185) and there is no alternative debug/test override or separate runtime source in the RTL that substitutes the delivered instruction.

concepts.concept: Instruction memory contents (the stored program words held by IMEM: writable RAM bytes mem_ram_b0..b3 or compiled ROM contents)
concepts.writers: RAM bytes mem_ram_b0..mem_ram_b3 are written from bus_req_i.data under the write condition if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1') (guard at line 114) with per-byte assigns at lines 116,119,122,125 (default) or 145,148,151,154 (alternative) and gated by byte-enable bits bus_req_i.ben(0..3) (lines 115/118/121/124 or 144/147/150/153). The ROM image mem_rom_c is a compile-time constant initialized at declaration (line 44) and is not written at runtime.
concepts.observers: The stored bytes are read into rdata (lines 128-131 in default style or 159-162 in alt_style) and thus are observable on the external response port bus_rsp_o.data when rden='1' (line 185).

confidentiality.reason: mem_ram_b0..b3 (written from bus_req_i.data under the write guard at line 114 and per-byte assigns at lines 116/119/122/125 or 145/148/151/154) are read into rdata (lines 128-131 or 159-162) and forwarded to the external bus via bus_rsp_o.data (line 185), so memory contents are observable and may be treated as confidential by the integrator.

integrity.reason: mem_ram_b* are updated from bus_req_i.data when (bus_req_i.stb='1') and (bus_req_i.rw='1') (guard at line 114 with per-byte writes at lines 116/119/122/125 and 145/148/151/154), so an external bus writer can modify stored program words; whether that writer is authorized depends on integration.

availability.reason: reading memory contents out is gated by rden which is set from bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (line 176) and bus_rsp_o.data is only driven when rden='1' (line 185), so external bus_req_i signals can prevent reads and deny progress.

undermined behavior.reason: mem_ram_b* are written only by the normal write path from bus_req_i.data (per-byte assigns at lines 116/119/122/125 and 145/148/151/154) and ROM contents are compile-time constant (line 44); the RTL contains no runtime debug/test override to substitute or bypass the stored contents.

concepts.concept: Bus acknowledge produced by IMEM (bus_rsp_o.ack) that reports request completion
concepts.writers: bus_rsp_o.ack is driven in the bus_feedback process: reset forces ack <= '0' (line 174); on rising clock the IMEM_INIT=true branch sets bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) (line 178) and the IMEM_INIT=false branch sets bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb (line 180).
concepts.observers: bus_rsp_o.ack is an external response port field (declaration line 31) and is observable outside the module whenever it is driven (assignments at lines 174, 178, 180).

confidentiality.reason: bus_rsp_o.ack is a protocol/status signal intended for the requester and in the IMEM_INIT=false branch is a direct copy of bus_req_i.stb (line 180), so it conveys no secret internal data.

integrity.reason: bus_rsp_o.ack is assigned from external request signals (ack <= bus_req_i.stb in the IMEM_INIT=false branch at line 180, or ack <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) at line 178), so an external requester can change the ack output by driving bus_req_i without internal protection.

availability.reason: the ack output is driven from bus_req_i.stb (and optionally bus_req_i.rw) per the assignment in the bus_feedback process (line 178/180), so external request signals can force or suppress ack and thereby affect availability of the bus handshake.

undermined behavior.reason: bus_rsp_o.ack has a single clocked driver in the bus_feedback process (assignments at lines 174, 178, 180) and there is no runtime debug/test override that replaces or bypasses ack generation.

concepts.concept: Read-enable decision (rden) that gates when rdata is forwarded to bus_rsp_o.data
concepts.writers: rden is reset to '0' on rstn_i='0' (line 173) and otherwise is clocked: rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) on the rising edge of clk (line 176) in the bus_feedback process.
concepts.observers: rden controls (gates) the external data output: bus_rsp_o.data <= rdata when (rden = '1') else (others => '0') (line 185), so the effect of rden is externally observable via bus_rsp_o.data (line 185).

confidentiality.reason: rden is computed directly from bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw (rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) at line 176) and its effect is visible on bus_rsp_o.data (line 185), so it reveals only request state, not secret data.

integrity.reason: rden is assigned from external request signals without additional protection (line 176) and it gates forwarding of rdata to the bus (line 185), so an external agent that controls bus_req_i can change rden while the forward is in use and influence what is delivered.

availability.reason: rden controls whether bus_rsp_o.data is driven (line 185) and rden itself is derived from bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw (line 176), so external bus_req_i signals can prevent reads and thus block progress.

undermined behavior.reason: rden has a single clocked driver in the bus_feedback process (line 176, reset at line 173) and there is no separate debug/test override path in the RTL.
